sentences.text: The case of the petitioners, in brief, is as follows:

On 21.12.2021 at about 11.40 a.m. the deceased was going towards Kolar from his village Ajjappanhalli by riding a Royal Enfield Bullet motor cycle bearing No. KA- 08-V-7973 and when he was going near Star chicken stall, on Bangarpet- Kolar road, the driver of KSRTC bus bearing No. KA-42-F-2038 came from same direction i.e.,
from Bangarpet side in a rash and negligent manner and while overtaking the deceased motor cycle lost control  3 SCCH-17 MVC No. 2011-2022 over his vehicle went to its wrong side of the road and dashed against the deceased motor cycle.
Due to the impact, the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident he was taken to S.N.R. Government Hospital, Kolar after first aid he was shifted to R.L. Jalappa Hospital, wherein he succumbed to the said injuries on the same day.
The petitioners have spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards funeral and other incidental expenses.

At the time of accident, the deceased was working as heavy motor vehicle driver and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m. and he was contributing the same to his family maintenance, but due to untimely death of deceased the petitioners have suffered mentally and physically.
The petitioners No.1 & 2 are the parents of the deceased Shashikumar, have lost love and affection and care taker.

In the Ex.R1 the driver of the bus bearing No. KA-42-F-2038 alleged that for the accident the negligence of the deceased is the sole  12 SCCH-17 MVC No. 2011-2022 reason.
But on considering the contents of Ex.P3 mahazar and rough sketch and the Ex.R2 photographs the accident has occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing no. KA-42-F-2038.

No evidence is available to disprove the contents of Ex.P3 and also there is no evidence is available to hold the contributory negligence or the negligence from the part of deceased for the said accident.

No doubt that in the claim petition the petitioners has to establish the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicles and also they are under the burden of establishing that the deceased or injured is not contributed towards the cause of negligence.
As discussed in Issue No.1, the contributory negligence of the deceased is not established before this tribunal.
The reasons discussed in issue No.1 shows the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending bus.
No evidence is placed by the respondent to discard the evidence of petitioners and to disbelieve the contents of police documents.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The petitioners have filed this petition U/s 166 of the Motor vehicles Act claiming compensation for the death of Shashikumar A.G., in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 21.12.2021.
On 21.12.2021 at about 11.40 a.m. the deceased was going towards Kolar from his village Ajjappanhalli by riding a Royal Enfield Bullet motor cycle bearing No. KA- 08-V-7973 and when he was going near Star chicken stall, on Bangarpet- Kolar road, the driver of KSRTC bus bearing No. KA-42-F-2038 came from same direction i.e.,
from Bangarpet side in a rash and negligent manner and while overtaking the deceased motor cycle lost control  3 SCCH-17 MVC No. 2011-2022 over his vehicle went to its wrong side of the road and dashed against the deceased motor cycle.
Due to the impact, the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
The respondent is the Shanthamma vs K.S.R.T.C on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168734160/
2  4 SCCH-17 MVC No. 2011-2022 owner cum insurer of the KSRTC bus bearing No. KA-42- F-2038 is liable to pay compensation compensation to the petitioners.
Hence the petitioners prays to award compensation of Rs.45,00,000/-
 3.
After service of notices the respondent appeared and filed written statement contending that the accident was occurred due to negligent riding of the motor cycle by the deceased himself and there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing No. KA-42-F- 2038.
Further contended that the accident was occurred due to negligence on the part of the deceased himself as he was riding the motor cycle in a rash and negligent manner and lost control over the vehicle and thrown from the motor cycle and came in contact with the bus near the foot board of the central door, which was proceeding on his side and exposed himself for the accident.
, though they  do not refer to the actual salary which was  being paid, keeping in view the factthat the  accident had occurred in the year 2012  and there was demand for drivers who  would drive such heavy-duty vehicles and  also the nature of duty involved, even if the  salary as stated is stated to be little on  exaggerated side, we can still assume it to  be Rs.20,000/- per month including daily  allowance.
If that is done and 40% of the  same is awarded towards `future  prospects', the same would in a sum of  Rs.28,000/-.
opennyai_summary.issue:
4. On the basis of the rival contentions, the following issues were framed by this court:
Shanthamma vs K.S.R.T.C on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168734160/
3  ISSUES  1) Whether the petitioners proves that  deceased Shashikumar A.G. died in the  motor vehicle accident that occurred on  21.12.2021 at about 11.40 a.m. on  Bangarpet- Kolar road, near Star Chicken  stall, at Kolar town and District, due to the  rash and negligence driving of the KSRTC  bus vehicle bearing No. KA-42-F-2038 by  its driver?
 2. Whether the petitioners prove that they are  the legal heirs and dependents of  deceased?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for  compensation?
If so, what amount and  from whom?
4 . What order or award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
But on considering the contents of Ex.P3 mahazar and rough sketch and the Ex.R2 photographs the accident has occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing no. KA-42-F-2038.
No evidence is available to disprove the contents of Ex.P3 and also there is no evidence is available to hold the contributory negligence or the negligence from the part of deceased for the said accident.
No doubt that there is no evidence is available to hold that the deceased was wearing helmet.
In the same way, the contents of police documents also silent in this regard to hold that the deceased was not wearing the helmet.
As per well settled position of law the standard of proof in claim petition like present one, is only preponderance of probabilities.
The respondent has not adduced any evidence to disprove the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.
By considering the same, no doubt that in the above quoted judgment the Hon'ble Supreme Court awarded the compensation by fixing the income of the driver of the heavy vehicle driver in the year 2012 at Rs.20,000/-.
27 . In Civil Special leave petition (Civil No.25590/2014 dated 31.10.2016 (National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi & others), the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that "While determining the income, in case the deceased was self-employed or  21 SCCH-17 MVC No. 2011-2022 on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
The respondent even though taken a contention of contributory negligence by the deceased,
the same is not established.
No doubt that in the claim petition the petitioners has to establish the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicles and also they are under the burden of establishing that the deceased or injured is not contributed towards the cause of negligence.
The reasons discussed in issue No.1 shows the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending bus.
No evidence is placed by the respondent to discard the evidence of petitioners and to disbelieve the contents of police documents.

The amount shall be deposited by the  19 SCCH-17 MVC No. 2011-2022  Respondent No.3-Insurance Company  within a period of six weeks from the date  of receipt of a copy of this judgment, where  upon the amount shall be disbursed to the  claimants.
The appeal is, accordingly, disposed of.
As per the above decisions 40% out of loss of dependency has to be granted towards future prospects which would Rs.8,64,000/-.
15 entitle for Rs.44,000/- for loss of consortium, further I inclined to award a sum of Rs.27,500/- towards loss of love and affection, Rs.16,500/- towards loss of estate and Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses (this amount is calculated as per Pranaya Sethi case with enhanced rate at 10% after three years).
The petitioners are entitled for compensation under the following heads:
1. Loss of dependency Rs. 21,60,000/-
2. Loss of future prospects Rs. 8,64,000/-
3. Loss of consortium Rs. 44,000/-
4. Loss of love and affection Rs. 27,500/-

No offences are invoked against the deceased by alleging the rash and negligent driving by the deceased hence, the said point raised by the respondent has holds no water.
The petitioners are entitle for the compensation along with the interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
34 . For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
 27 SCCH-17 MVC No. 2011-2022  ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s. 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioners No.1 & 2 are entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.31,28,500/-(Rupees Thirty one lakhs twenty eight thousand five hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
The petitioners No.1 & 2 are entitled for the compensation at the ratio of 60:40.
Out of total compensation awarded to the Petitioners, 50% of shall released in favour petitioner No.1 and 2, on their proper identification and remaining 50% shall be 28 SCCH-17 MVC No. 2011-2022 kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years, in their names.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw the award accordingly.
